citations.quote: MANILA — Sen. Robin Padilla on Wednesday questioned state auditor Roderick Wamil on his familiarity with terrorism and with security threats as he stressed the importance of confidential funds to address these issues.
Padilla asked Wamil if he had been to parts of the country like the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao, the Bicol region, and to Mindanao.
Padilla also asked Wamil if he had visited remote communities and seen the challenges faced by residents there, including access to food and medicine.

citations.quote: Wamil, previously assigned to the Commission on Audit-Internal Control and Fraud Audit Office, was testifying at the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte on audit findings on her offices' use of confidential funds.

MANILA, Philippines — Senators allied with Vice President Sara Duterte questioned the testimony of Roderick Wamil of the Commission on Audit, with minority member Robinhood Padilla even claiming that the confidential funds were spent to quash communist rebellion.

Padilla claimed that these checks – P125 million dated Dec. 20, 2022, P125 million for Jan. 31, 2023, and P125 million for April 18, 2023 – were near key anniversary dates of the Communist Party of the Philippines (CPP), National Democratic Front (NDF) and New People’s Army (NPA).
He implied that the Vice President’s confidential funds were used to prevent any communist attacks during those dates.
